_comment: Second-host probes for road-to-skills-that-arrive-when-called 0.3, in the row shape of skill-lifecycle-probes.json (validated by recordProblems in src/scripts/_lib/injection_effect.ts). Every probe ran `codex exec` in a scratch project whose `.agents/skills` held only zz-*-probe skills; the user roots were the maintainer's real ones, so the omitted counts include them. Transcripts are machine-local rollout files under ~/.codex/sessions and are named, not committed. Phase 4 of the roadmap is gated on these rows for this host.

live-pickup-agents-skills.reason: Probe: a session writes a skill under the repo's `.agents/skills` mid-turn and is asked whether its system-supplied listing now carries it. Four attempts on 2026-10-19 under codex-cli 0.148.0 did not reach an answer: the first stopped on a coordination question the package's own global instructions raised, the next three ended `429 Too Many Requests` after the session start — the subscription's rate limit, so a later run can take it. The host page says changes are detected automatically and to restart if one does not appear; that is documentation, not an observation. Re-tried 2026-10-20 under codex-cli 0.148.0 with the probe reshaped so the write comes from OUTSIDE the session mid-turn (the session sleeps, a second process writes `.agents/skills/zz-late-probe`), because a probe that writes its own skill cannot run: the sandbox reports `.agents` read-only under `-s workspace-write` (session 01a156f2-4cee-74e1-ae05-c3ff3d558dd6), so the host protects the very directory the probe must write. That run stopped on the same coordination question the package's own global instructions raise; a third run with the question pre-answered (session 01a156f2-e055-7161-aebb-94ba36ab63fb) ended `429 Too Many Requests` at the subscription's rate limit before the sleep, the second rate-limited day in a row. Two things were observed on the way and are not the cell: a skill present only under the repo's `.agents/skills` IS listed (`BEFORE: zz-early-probe`), and the omission warning fired at 426 omitted skills on this machine's real user roots. The cell stays `unobserved`: a host-side rate limit is a wait, not a reading.

omission-order-and-warning.reason: Verbatim warning on stderr: `warning: Exceeded skills context budget. All skill descriptions were removed and 554 additional skills were not included in the model-visible skills list.` With 120 repo-scope probe skills the injected list held 347 entries: the 5 system skills first, then all 120 repo-scope skills, then the user roots (`~/.codex/skills`, `~/.agents/skills`) in name order, cut off at `guideline-writing`. So descriptions go first and as a block, then entries are dropped from the alphabetical tail of the user scope while system and repo scope survive whole.

implicit-disabled-counts-against-budget.reason: Same 120 repo-scope skills, 60 of them with `agents/openai.yaml` `policy: allow_implicit_invocation: false`. The 60 disabled ones left the model-visible list entirely, the omitted count fell from 554 to 481 and the list grew from 347 to 355 entries. A skill with implicit invocation disabled is not listed and does not occupy the budget — a resident set can be enforced by disabling implicit invocation for everything outside it.

double-listing.reason: The host does not read `.claude/skills`: a probe skill placed only there in the repo was reported not available. It does read `~/.codex/skills` beside the documented `~/.agents/skills`, and a skill present under both is listed twice (every user-scope entry in both sessions appears once per root, 111 and 145 pairs) — the host never merges same-name skills, so a package that writes both roots spends the budget twice.

unlisted-skill-not-in-model-list.transcript: ~/.codex/sessions/2026/10/20/ rollout for session 01a15751-db98-7523-a93d-c9fc3605aead; paired with 01a1573b-c7bb-7450-afca-6091f998cbe4 and 01a15755-42d0-7752-9404-8d3f27447275
unlisted-skill-not-in-model-list.reason: Two-armed, taken for 5.2's arm S3 and then for the blocker `second-host-unlisted-reachability`. Under a scratch `HOME` and `CODEX_HOME` carrying the resident set of 4.1, asked which of two names are in its skills list, the session answered `RESIDENT=YES` for a resident skill and `NONRESIDENT=NO` for `docker`, which is installed on disk and carries `agents/openai.yaml` with `policy.allow_implicit_invocation: false`. Asked to INVOKE the non-resident one it answered `UNAVAILABLE` and made no tool call; asked to invoke the resident one it did not use the skill mechanism either, it `sed`-read the file it knew the path to. So what is established is narrower than `the host refuses an invocation` and wider than `nothing changed`: a policy-disabled skill is NOT in the model-visible skills list, and a model that cannot see it does not reach for it. Its body stays readable by a caller that already knows the path, which is a filesystem read and not the skill mechanism. Consequence: `unlisted` remains the factually correct bucket (installed, not listed) and must not be read as `reachable`.

unlisted-skill-reached-through-finder.transcript: scratch CODEX_HOME rollouts for sessions 01a15902-c78d-7aa3-a5cf-8af3541c2c52 (named), 01a15909-e404-7620-a795-25a15790880f (search-read), 01a1590a-35ac-7772-acc6-a015728db02e (unknown name), with 01a15902-2356-7a70-bc4f-86c28634249b (listing) and 01a15909-9e93-7181-8cc0-2450cb989e82 (unprompted)
unlisted-skill-reached-through-finder.reason: Remedy (a) of `second-host-unlisted-reachability`. With the resident set of 4.1 plus the installer-written `agent-config-skill-finder` entry, the finder is in the model-visible list and `docker` is not, with no omission warning. Asked to use `docker` by name, the session read the finder and then `cat` the non-resident SKILL.md and followed an instruction on its last line; asked to find and follow the fitting package skill for a task, it ran `agent-config route:explain --skills`, read `sql-writing` whole and followed its last-line instruction; an unknown name was refused with the nearest real names. A first named run that did a ranged read missed the last line, which is why the finder now prescribes a whole-file read. Not observed: a model given an ordinary task with nothing pointing at skills consulted no skill at all, finder included — the `model-suggested` path 4.2 does not count. Full record: agents/evidence/analysis/second-host-finder-probe-20261020.md.
